explanation: Tipton dissent (not the majority) cites Sainz in 1980 as showing New Mexico decides entrapment objectively as a matter of law; Fiechter (1976) overruled Sainz on exactly that government-conduct focus; no negative history noted; unrelated Illinois case.

Von Hofe quotes Grady only for the general maxim that a problem's severity cannot excuse adherence to constitutional principles; Dixon overruled Grady's same-conduct double jeopardy test, a different point, so limb 1 fails.

McNair cites Schuessler for the point that mental disease does not itself establish legal insanity; Meraz overruled Schuessler only on the appellate standard for reviewing affirmative-defense findings, a different point.

Gray cites Collins for no entitlement to a decision-maker of one's own race; Brooks disapproved Collins's holding that purposeful inclusion of Negroes invalidates an indictment, and itself reaffirmed that proportional representation is not required; different point.

Julien quotes Bourque (through Wells) only for deference to trial-court credibility findings; Comeaux overruled Bourque's limit on penalty-phase evidence of unadjudicated crimes, an unrelated point, so limb 1 fails.

Tulsa Hotel disapproved Dunkelberger's latent-injury limitations rule, but Auclair only recites it as the employee's argument (noting an earlier Rhode Island quotation) and decides on its own statute's knew-or-should-have-known text; no reliance.

Brown footnote lists Reliance among Board decisions holding section 283(f) confirmed Board jurisdiction; Art Metal overruled Reliance on whether collection was time-barred under the 1921/1924 Acts, a different point, so limb 1 fails.
